title: A film one worker cannot keep at real time is shared with every worker that has room, with no room held back for a viewer who has not asked
description: JS-162: with two equal workers no helper ever starts; the server refused one 302 to 304 times per play, every time for the room it keeps for a new viewer, with one viewer and nothing queued, and the film stalled exactly as on one worker. With that rule lifted (measurement build) two workers held 1.00x until the seek and three held it throughout; a small worker's job was carried by a large worker's helper. The room for the next viewer is the operator's and the autoscaler's to keep (docs/transcoding.md's sizing advice, JS-164, JS-057), not a rule that idles a worker beside a stalling film. Takes BL-242. D-046.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed first with real processes and recorded: two equal workers and one viewer of a re-encode each makes under 0.9 times real time: the helpers refused, by rule. The check that follows fails today.

A helper is queued and claimed whenever a worker has the cores for it; the room kept for a viewer who has not asked is gone at the insert and at the claim. A helper still never takes a worker over its cores, and workers deciding together still never take the same last cores (two real workers, contended).

Two equal workers each making the job under 0.9 times real time, in jellyfin-web, with and without a burned-in PGS track: 10 minutes from the start, a seek to the middle, 10 minutes more. In each part: speed at or above 1.0 after its first 30 seconds, no more than 3 freezes of 0.5 seconds or more per 10 minutes, none over 2 seconds (JS-162 measured 1.00x and 3 freezes before the seek with the rule lifted; after the seek is this task's to show, with JS-167). Run three times; every run within the bound. If two workers cannot hold it after the seek, the figures come back as a brief and nothing is weakened. These long runs are a recorded measurement on the build, not a locked check; the locked check is the short form: with two throttled workers and a fixture film, a helper starts within 10 seconds of the job being judged slow, and again within 10 seconds of a seek.
One 2-CPU and one 6-CPU worker with the viewer's job on the 2-CPU one: the same bound, throughout.

Observed and recorded, not yet changed: a second viewer arrives while helpers hold every worker. Measured in jellyfin-web, three times each for a second play of the same cost and a 1080p SDR one: the second viewer's time to first frame against the same play on an idle cluster, and the first viewer's speed and freezes for 5 minutes after. The figures come to the product owner as a brief before JS-161's Spec: D-046 states who gives way as a default (JS-161 criterion 11), and these figures confirm it or change it.

With transcodeHelpers off nothing changes. With one worker nothing changes: no helper is queued or claimed, whatever cores the worker has free, and every check that passed on 30af59c passes unamended, but for the 16-core subcase of the helper capacity check, which gains a second worker (D-053), and the setup of the cross-version subtest 'an idle worker of another version does not count as a slot for a viewer', whose helper now runs on a second worker of the version, with its assertions kept and one added: the helper is stopped when the third viewer asks, not by the half-timeout rescue (D-054). A helper is never claimed by a worker that is at that moment running a viewer's, a seek's or a failover's job of its spec. A worker running only helpers of that spec may still take another when it has the cores, after the one-second wait, as before (a dead helper's replacement). Checked with real processes: one worker with cores for three jobs and two viewers of one spec has one job; two workers, the viewers' job on one, has its helper on the other in 10 of 10 (D-052).
No start of play and no seek is slower for a lone viewer: time to first segment measured before and after.

docs/transcoding.md, docs/status.md and DOMAINS.md invariant 58 are updated; docs/running.md keeps the advice to run with the dearest film's cores to spare and says the server no longer holds that room itself; listed under Changed guarantees citing D-046.
